title: Infinite Slope — Submerged with Seepage
applicability: Seepage parallel to slope surface. γ'/γ_sat ≈ 0.5 for typical soils.

title: Infinite Slope — General (c', φ', u)
equation: FS = c'/(γz sinβ cosβ) + tanφ'/tanβ - u tanφ'/(γz sinβ cosβ)

title: Bishop's Simplified Method
equation: FS = Σ{[c'b + (W - ub)tanφ'] / m_α} / Σ(W sinα)

u.description: Pore pressure at slice base center

α.description: Inclination of slice base from horizontal

applicability: Circular surfaces. Iterative solution. Excellent accuracy (±1-2% of rigorous).

title: Ordinary Method of Slices (Fellenius)
equation: FS = Σ[c'Δl + (W cosα - uΔl)tanφ'] / Σ(W sinα)
applicability: Non-iterative but underestimates FS by 10-15% for deep circles with high pore pressure. Use Bishop instead.

title: Undrained FS (φ = 0, Circular Surface)
equation: FS = s_u × R × θ / Σ(W × d)

d.description: Horizontal distance from slice center to center of rotation

title: Pore Pressure Ratio

γ.description: Total unit weight of soil above

applicability: r_u = 0: dry. r_u ≈ 0.5: WT at surface with parallel seepage.

title: Pseudostatic Seismic Force
equation: F_h = k_h × W; F_v = k_v × W
applicability: Typical k_h = 0.05–0.25. Pseudostatic FS ≥ 1.0–1.1 is acceptable (transient loading).

title: Taylor's Stability Charts (φ = 0)
equation: s_u / (FS × γ × H) = N_s (stability number from chart)
applicability: Quick estimate for homogeneous slopes in undrained conditions. Look up N_s from Taylor's chart using slope angle.

title: Critical Height (Vertical Cut, φ = 0)
equation: H_c = 4 × s_u / γ (unsupported) or H_c = 3.83 × s_u / γ (with tension crack)

H_c.description: Maximum height of unsupported vertical cut
